intro.title: ADRs, Technical Debt & Estimation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn foundational concepts for leading technical projects: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), Technical Debt, and Estimation. You will not write code, but instead build a conceptual framework by creating a simple ADR template, analyzing a technical debt scenario, and practicing a basic estimation technique. The core concepts involve structured documentation, risk assessment, and planning. You will use markdown-like templates and decision logs as the main constructs. This will help you communicate decisions, manage trade-offs, and set realistic timelines in a team environment.
intro.usecase: In real-world software engineering, ADRs, technical debt management, and estimation are critical for product planning and team alignment. For example, when building a new feature like a user dashboard, an ADR documents the decision to use a specific charting library, while technical debt tracking might flag legacy code in the dashboard's data-fetching layer. Estimation helps teams scope sprints for adding interactive filters or modals to this dashboard, ensuring realistic timelines and resource allocation. These practices are visible in product roadmaps, backlog grooming sessions, and architecture review meetings, directly impacting feature delivery and system maintainability.
